| [![arXiv](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-2610.41895-b31b1b.svg)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.41895) | **The 943 MHz radio-SFR relation of nearby galaxies observed with ASKAP**  |
|| S. Wang, et al. -- incl., <mark>J. Li</mark> |
|*Appeared on*| *2026-11-02*|
|*Comments*| *15 pages, 9 Figures, and 1 Table, accepted for publication in APJ*|
|**Abstract**|            We investigate the integrated 943 MHz radio-infrared and radio-star-formation-rate (SFR) relations of 875 nearby galaxies within $D<50$ Mpc using public Australian SKA Pathfinder (ASKAP) observations. After excluding galaxies with identified or candidate AGN activity, 594 galaxies remain in the AGN-cleaned sample. We used Bayesian errors-in-variables models that account for measurement uncertainties, intrinsic scatter, and correlated distance errors. The AGN-cleaned radio-infrared relation is nearly linear, $L_{\nu,943}\propto L_{\nu,\mathrm{W4}}^{1.09\pm0.02}$, with an orthogonal intrinsic scatter of $0.21\pm0.01$ dex, and is tighter than the AGN-host relation. For 592 AGN-cleaned galaxies, the radio-SFR relation is approximately linear, $L_{\nu,943}\propto{\rm SFR}^{1.02\pm0.02}$, with an intrinsic scatter of $0.25\pm0.01$ dex. Semi-calorimetric models reveal positive secondary dependences on stellar mass, $\gamma=0.09\pm0.03$, and rotation velocity, $\delta=0.24\pm0.08$. The consistency between these two secondary trends suggests that the galaxy gravitational potential may weakly regulate CRE confinement and synchrotron-radiation efficiency. Our results provide an integrated 943 MHz radio-SFR calibration for nearby galaxies and show that, although radio luminosity scales nearly proportionally with SFR on average, weak secondary dependences on galaxy properties remain.         |
